title: AI moves beyond pilot phase for Aussie businesses: Deloitte
full_text:
Australian organisations are making "real progress" in their artificial intelligence (AI) adoption as it shortens decision cycles, accelerates execution and drives workplace redesign, according to a study by Deloitte.
Organisations are no longer deploying AI as part of their technology stack but are redesigning work around AI, Deloitte finds in its newly published report State of AI in the Enterprise.
The survey of 3500 global leaders found that 39% of the Australian cohort are redesigning several key processes around AI, while 73% expect it to handle the majority of tasks in routine knowledge work within three years.
AI is not only shortening decision cycles and producing more measurable results, it is also transforming jobs, and increasingly moving into physical operations.
Currently, 38% of Australian organisations allow AI to act autonomously without human approval to a moderate degree. At the same time, 18% said accountability is unclear when an AI system produces a negative outcome.
Of all the leaders surveyed, 81% said AI has improved the speed of decision-making and execution, making faster decisions one of AI's most widespread benefits. Yet only 25% are using AI for deep transformation such as creating new products or services, reengineering core processes or fundamentally reinventing their business model.
"Across most industries, faster decision-making falls within a narrow band of 78% to 82%, with financial services at the low end of that range and technology and energy tied at the top of it. The spread is too tight to call a real pattern - speed has become a common benefit of AI, not one limited to a particular type of company," Deloitte said.
As AI threatens to snare many jobs, the report found that the work itself is changing, but full transformation remains rare.
Nearly two thirds (60%) of all organisations have already redesigned jobs around AI capabilities to at least a moderate degree. However, only 15% described those changes as "extensive or complete."
Meanwhile, most Australian leaders (86%) expect their organisation's AI capability to increase moderately or significantly over the next 12 months. They also reported increased revenue gains from AI, rising from 20% in January to currently 27%.
"Amid this scale of investment, the total bill has become the most closely watched measure of AI economics: 71% of companies track total spend on AI inference and API consumption, the highest level of tracking across the metrics in the survey. That holds across industries, with technology, media and telecom leading at 75%," the report read.
